rationale:
The fix commit 5d4f6b8 (PR #229, subject 'Index out of range during parsing Crash Fix') explicitly cites issue 225 in its message ('https://github.com/swiftlang/swift-markdown/issues/225 Fix for crash'), and traceability.verified_fix_issue_numbers=[225] via path fix_commit_to_issue. The defect is a line-splitting mismatch: LazySplitLines split source only on '
', so carriage-return line endings that cmark treats as line breaks produced inconsistent line indices during parsing (index out of range). The minimized production patch retains exactly one semantic hunk in Sources/Markdown/Parser/LazySplitLines.swift replacing split(separator: "
", maxSplits: Int.max, omittingEmptySubsequences: false) with split(omittingEmptySubsequences: false, whereSeparator: \.isNewline); no formatting, docs, config, or test content remains. Notably the BlockDirective.swift hunk of the original commit was largely a reindentation and was removed by minimization (3 of 4 hunks removed, post_minimization_validation=PASS). The trigger is the unchanged upstream test DocumentTests.testParseNewlineCharacters, which parses a document containing '
', '', and '
' terminators through the pre-existing public API Document(parsing:options:) and debugDescription(); it introduces no API added by the fix. Machine evidence in strict_post_minimization shows build.both_versions PASS, trigger.buggy_differential reproducing only 'DocumentTests.swift::testParseNewlineCharacters', trigger.fixed_clean PASS, trigger.deterministic across 3 repetitions, and full_suite.fixed_all_green with buggy failures limited to the reproduced trigger. active_same_project_root_causes is empty, so swiftlang/swift-markdown#225 is not a duplicate and matches allowed_root_cause_ids.

Single fixing commit 5d4f6b8 (PR #229) is titled 'Index out of range during parsing Crash Fix' and its body links issue #225; traceability records path fix_commit_to_issue with verified_fix_issue_numbers=[225], and #225 is the allowed verified key. The defect is pre-existing line-splitting behavior: the parser split source text only on '
', so ''/'
' terminated lines were not treated as line breaks, desynchronizing swift-markdown's line array from cmark's line/column reporting. The minimized production patch retains exactly one hunk, Sources/Markdown/Parser/LazySplitLines.swift changing input.split(separator: "
", ...) to split(omittingEmptySubsequences: false, whereSeparator: \.isNewline) — one behavioral line, no formatting-only, doc-only, config-only or test-only content; the three cosmetic/secondary hunks (BlockDirective re-indentation, BlockDirectiveParser, MarkupFormatter) were removed by minimization and post_minimization_validation is PASS. The trigger is the unchanged upstream test from the same fixing commit (DocumentTests.testParseNewlineCharacters), which parses a document mixing 
,  and 
 through the pre-existing Document(parsing:options:) API and asserts the heading tree, so it introduces no fix-added production API. Machine strict evidence for both the original and post-minimization states shows build passing on both revisions, isolated buggy failure of the declared trigger, the non-reproducing selector testParseURL passing, deterministic outcomes over 3 repetitions (38 matrix runs), and a fully green fixed full suite. active_same_project_root_causes is empty, so this root cause is not a registry duplicate.

The retained single hunk fixes the parser path only; the three remaining call sites (BlockDirective, BlockDirectiveParser, MarkupFormatter) keep '\n'-only splitting at the buggy-plus-minimized-fix state, so residual carriage-return handling defects outside Document parsing are not covered by this case.

The trigger asserts debugDescription equality rather than explicitly asserting absence of a crash, so the observed buggy failure mode is inferred from the runtime differential gate rather than from an assertion naming the index-out-of-range crash.
trigger_tests declares a second selector (testParseURL) that does not reproduce the defect; only testParseNewlineCharacters is the defect-specific trigger.
Evidence grade is portable_release_evidence with full_suite_repetitions=1, so flakiness outside the 3-repetition trigger matrix is only weakly bounded.
